heading: Security rules for browser code
body: Never put server credentials (passwords, keys or tokens for the server) in Tac configuration or adapters. Browser HTTP still follows origin and CORS (cross-origin resource sharing) rules. HTTP request annotations require these things: no credentials sent, redirects rejected, cancellation, a deadline and a limited response. Behavior caches are separate from two other caches. These are the limited JSON response cache of HTTPClient and the read cache of the service worker. Divide the cache by the signed-in user who owns the data. Authorize every cache access, including hits (reads that find an entry) and eviction (removal of an entry). Choose an adapter that enforces the declared limit on entries (the entry quota). Browser code cannot replace authorization on the server. The API must still check access to sensitive data. An annotation grants no native capability, database connection, environment access or server-side rendering (SSR) mode. The build refuses a secret in page code or in `client/manifest.json` (`TY1324`), `eval` and `new Function` (`TY1325`), and a request to a host that `tac.outgoing.hosts` does not list (`TY1326`); the page's `connect-src` enforces the same list in the browser (ADR 0068).
